About this map
Rule of time: solid through the years Scripture states a fact; after that a people holds its place, striped (inferred), until Scripture has it replaced, ended or renewed, and at the latest until its last mention in the Bible Inventory; a king only while he is stated. Israel and its fathers: one colour at each stated place, journeying to the next along Scripture's route where it names one; a dashed edge where the years there are inferred. The cities Israel took and did not burn are in Israel's colour from the taking until the tribes' towns are shown (Jericho, Ai and Hazor were burned: Joshua 6:24; 8:28; 11:11-13). In the land, each tribe's towns in its own shade (the towns of its lot in the Inventory), the Levites' cities ringed, the towns Scripture says were not driven out left to those who remained; the allotment's borders from the Joshua 13-21 Allotment Map v08. The colour stops at the sea and the lakes. The other peoples' colours are provisional. The Egyptians' area is drawn as the Joshua 13-21 Allotment Map draws a tribe, in its yellow: strongest beside the border, fading inward; east to the Red Sea and the lakes of the Isthmus; to the west, where the limit is unknown, fading out with no line (its outline otherwise OpenBible's, the middle of its confidence bands, rounded off). The land of Canaan in Abram's days, where the Canaanites and the Perizzites dwelt (Genesis 13:7), is drawn the same way in one colour, the two named in it: strongest along the Great Sea's shore and down the Jordan to the Salt Sea (Numbers 34:6, 12), fading inward; to the north and the south, where its limit is unknown, fading out. The cities of the plain (Genesis 13:12; 19:29) are drawn the same way along their valley: the ground below 250 m under sea level south of the Salt Sea as the Base Map draws it about 2000 BC (on the Base Map's heights, from the Copernicus model credited below), strongest along the valley's edge, with a line just inside it, fading to its middle. The events listed are those whose place blinks on the map in view, and every turn of Israel's way, each as its journey starts. The map follows Israel: when the next stop lies off the screen it zooms out to show both, the line runs, and it zooms in to the new stop. The route drawn is the traditional southern route; others are proposed. Names: the Base Map's lettering as data (its windows of 09/30/2026: B-3 f1 to C-4 c1 and A-2 e1 to B-3 c2 at 1:1,000,000, A-1 a1 to C-4 f4 at 1:2,500,000, A-1 a1 to G-6 f4 at 1:5,000,000; Rameses, Pithom, Succoth and Zoan, places later than c. 2000 BC, set by the Base Map for this map alone), each shown from the event Scripture names it at, or from the place's first mention, until it is renamed; dimmed where Scripture has the place destroyed (until built again) or burned (for 100 years). Years from the Bible Inventory. Names called out as Play runs: the place as the verse names it, the name of the time under it. Scripture taken from the New King James Version®.
